scope: Numbers 3–4, all 100 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 3–4. All 100 exact original records are hashed, including annotations at 3:30 and 3:39, with the extraordinary dots on and Aaron retained in the original bytes. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Renders toledot as family record, connecting the heading to Genesis while retaining both Aaron and Moses and the Sinai setting.
verses.before: These are the generations of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
verses.after: This is the family record of Aaron and Moses at the time the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the generations of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

verses.rationale: Presents all four sons in order and keeps firstborn attached specifically to Nadab.
verses.before: These are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.after: Aaron’s sons were named Nadab, the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

verses.rationale: Unfolds filling the hand as ordination without naming an unstated agent; retains anointing and the repeated priestly role.
verses.before: These are the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.
verses.after: These were Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests who were ordained to serve as priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.

verses.rationale: Keeps death, unauthorized fire, absence of sons and the two surviving priests; preserves in-the-presence wording with its lifetime sense noted.
verses.before: Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
verses.after: But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they presented unauthorized fire before him in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of their father Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.

verses.rationale: Introduces the distinct instruction to Moses without absorbing it into the genealogy.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves drawing near, standing before Aaron and service to him, rather than making all Levites priests.
verses.before: “Bring the tribe of Levi near and set them before Aaron the priest so that they may serve him.
verses.after: “Bring the tribe of Levi near and have them stand before Aaron the priest to serve him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Bring the tribe of Levi near and set them before Aaron the priest so that they may serve him.

verses.rationale: Makes both Aaron and the community beneficiaries of the entrusted duties and retains the sanctuary location and work.
verses.before: They will keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the Tent of Meeting, performing the service of the tabernacle.
verses.after: They are to carry out the duties owed to him and to the whole community before the tent of meeting, doing the work of the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the Tent of Meeting, performing the service of the tabernacle.

verses.rationale: Retains the full furnishings, Israel’s charge and repeated tabernacle work while clarifying the relation between them.
verses.before: They will keep all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting and the charge of the Israelites by performing the service of the tabernacle.
verses.after: They are to care for all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and fulfill the Israelites’ responsibilities by doing the work of the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall keep all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting and the charge of the Israelites by performing the service of the tabernacle.

verses.rationale: Keeps the giving language, the repeated-given emphasis, Aaron and his sons followed by singular him, and the Israelite origin.
verses.before: You will give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are wholly given to him from among the Israelites.
verses.after: Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They are given entirely to him from among the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are wholly given to him from among the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes priestly responsibility from Levitical service and retains the death penalty; unauthorized describes access rather than ethnicity.
verses.before: You will appoint Aaron and his sons, and they will keep their priesthood. Any outsider who approaches will be put to death.”
verses.after: Appoint Aaron and his sons to keep charge of their priesthood. Any unauthorized person who comes near must be put to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood. Any outsider who approaches shall be put to death.”

verses.rationale: Retains the new speech boundary before the firstborn substitution explanation.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic divine agency, substitution and the womb-opening image; links belonging to the reason in the next verse.
verses.before: “Look, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites will be mine,
verses.after: “Look, I myself have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among them. The Levites will belong to me,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites shall be mine,

verses.rationale: Keeps the causal link, actual deaths in Egypt, consecration of both humans and animals, and repeated claim of belonging.
verses.before: for every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They will be mine. I am the LORD.”
verses.after: because every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I made every firstborn in Israel holy for myself, human and animal alike. They will belong to me. I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: for every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They shall be mine. I am the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated Sinai location as the next census instruction begins.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,
verses.after: In the wilderness of Sinai, the LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the two kinship levels in source order and the male one-month threshold, distinct from the military census.
verses.before: “Count the Levites by their ancestral houses and clans. Every male from one month old and upward you will count.”
verses.after: “Register Levi’s descendants by ancestral household and clan. Count every male one month old and upward.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Count the Levites by their ancestral houses and clans. Every male from one month old and upward you shall count.”

verses.rationale: Renders at-the-mouth idiom as direction and preserves both the action and explicit obedience.
verses.before: So Moses counted them according to the word of the LORD, as he was commanded.
verses.after: Moses registered them at the LORD’s direction, just as he had been commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses counted them according to the word of the LORD, as he was commanded.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three founding sons in order before their descendant clans are listed.
verses.before: These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.after: Levi’s sons were named Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

verses.rationale: Clarifies how the sons’ names relate to the clans while retaining both personal names.
verses.before: These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
verses.after: Gershon’s sons, whose names identify their clans, were Libni and Shimei.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four sons in order and the clan organization without conflating them with later leaders.
verses.before: The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
verses.after: Kohath’s sons, by their clans, were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

verses.rationale: Retains both sons and the closing summary’s clan and household levels.
verses.before: The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of Levi by their ancestral houses.
verses.after: Merari’s sons, by their clans, were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans, grouped by ancestral household.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of Levi by their ancestral houses.

verses.rationale: Makes the personal-name-to-clan relationship explicit and retains the repeated group summary.
verses.before: From Gershon came the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these were the clans of the Gershonites.
verses.after: Gershon’s descendants formed the Libnite and Shimeite clans. These were the Gershonite clans.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Gershon came the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these were the clans of the Gershonites.

verses.rationale: Preserves the male and age scope and exact Gershonite count without treating it as the service-age count in chapter 4.
verses.before: Those counted among them, by the number of all males from one month old and upward, were seven thousand five hundred.
verses.after: Their registered males, counting everyone one month old and upward, numbered 7,500.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those counted among them, by the number of all males from one month old and upward, were seven thousand five hundred.

verses.rationale: Keeps both rear and west as the clan’s spatial placement.
verses.before: The clans of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle on the west.
verses.after: The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
verses.tsw_comparator: The clans of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle on the west.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named leader and father and avoids confusing this Eliasaph with Gad’s leader in chapters 1–2.
verses.before: The leader of the ancestral house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
verses.after: Eliasaph son of Lael was the leader of the Gershonites’ ancestral household.
verses.tsw_comparator: The leader of the ancestral house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.

verses.rationale: Retains the overlapping sanctuary terms and all listed coverings, continuing the inventory into verse 26.
verses.before: The charge of the Gershonites in the Tent of Meeting was the tabernacle, the tent with its covering, the screen for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
verses.after: In the tent of meeting, the Gershonites were responsible for the tabernacle and tent, its covering, the entrance screen of the tent of meeting,
verses.tsw_comparator: The charge of the Gershonites in the Tent of Meeting was the tabernacle, the tent with its covering, the screen for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,

verses.rationale: Keeps courtyard, entrance, tabernacle, altar, ropes and service; does not omit the inventory’s less prominent items.
verses.before: the hangings of the court, the screen for the entrance of the court around the tabernacle and altar, and its cords—all the service connected with them.
verses.after: and the courtyard hangings, the entrance screen of the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar, its ropes and all the work connected with these things.
verses.tsw_comparator: the hangings of the court, the screen for the entrance of the court around the tabernacle and altar, and its cords—all the service connected with them.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four clan names and the closing group identification in the same pattern as Gershon.
verses.before: From Kohath came the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites, and the clan of the Uzzielites; these were the clans of the Kohathites.
verses.after: Kohath’s descendants formed the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite and Uzzielite clans. These were the Kohathite clans.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Kohath came the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites, and the clan of the Uzzielites; these were the clans of the Kohathites.

verses.rationale: Retains 8600 as the pinned Hebrew reads, despite the discrepancy with the chapter’s stated total; keeps the sanctuary charge.
verses.before: By the number of all males from one month old and upward, there were eight thousand six hundred, keeping charge of the sanctuary.
verses.after: Counting every male one month old and upward, they numbered 8,600. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the number of all males from one month old and upward, there were eight thousand six hundred, keeping charge of the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Preserves the descendant relationship and southern placement beside the tabernacle.
verses.before: The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
verses.after: The clans descended from Kohath were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.

verses.rationale: Retains the leader and father with the clan/household relationship; the source annotation is included in the exact hash.
verses.before: The leader of the ancestral house of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
verses.after: Elizaphan son of Uzziel was the leader of the ancestral household of the Kohathite clans.
verses.tsw_comparator: The leader of the ancestral house of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural altars and every inventory category; does not assign the utensils’ priestly use to all Kohathites.
verses.before: Their charge was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the vessels of the sanctuary with which the priests minister, the screen, and all the service connected with them.
verses.after: They were responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the sacred utensils used in service, the screen and all the work connected with these things.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their charge was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the vessels of the sanctuary with which the priests minister, the screen, and all the service connected with them.

verses.rationale: Makes the leader-of-leaders relationship clear while preserving his patronymic and separate oversight duty.
verses.before: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest was chief over the leaders of the Levites and had oversight of those keeping charge of the sanctuary.
verses.after: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest was chief over the Levite leaders. He oversaw those responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest was chief over the leaders of the Levites and had oversight of those keeping charge of the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Retains both clan names and the repeated identification of their parent group.
verses.before: From Merari came the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites; these were the clans of Merari.
verses.after: Merari’s descendants formed the Mahlite and Mushite clans. These were the Merarite clans.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Merari came the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites; these were the clans of Merari.

verses.rationale: Preserves the exact Merarite total with the same sex and age criteria as the other chapter 3 counts.
verses.before: Those counted among them, by the number of all males from one month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.
verses.after: Their registered males, counting everyone one month old and upward, numbered 6,200.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those counted among them, by the number of all males from one month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.

verses.rationale: Keeps leader, father, family grouping and northern placement without merging the personal and camp information.
verses.before: The leader of the ancestral house of the clans of Merari was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
verses.after: Zuriel son of Abihail was the leader of the ancestral household of the Merarite clans. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: The leader of the ancestral house of the clans of Merari was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.

verses.rationale: Retains each structural component and the comprehensive equipment/service clauses; frames follows the revised Exodus terminology.
verses.before: The appointed charge of the Merarites was the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars, bases, all its equipment, and all the service connected with them,
verses.after: The Merarites were assigned responsibility for the tabernacle’s frames, crossbars, pillars, bases and all its equipment, with all the work connected with these things,
verses.tsw_comparator: The appointed charge of the Merarites was the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars, bases, all its equipment, and all the service connected with them,

verses.rationale: Completes the inventory without omitting courtyard supports or the small transport components.
verses.before: together with the pillars around the court, their bases, pegs, and cords.
verses.after: as well as the pillars around the courtyard, their bases, pegs and ropes.
verses.tsw_comparator: together with the pillars around the court, their bases, pegs, and cords.

verses.rationale: Clarifies whose sons are meant, retains both eastern expressions and Israel’s charge, and keeps the actual penalty.
verses.before: Those camping in front of the tabernacle on the east, before the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and Aaron’s sons, keeping charge of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who approached was to be put to death.
verses.after: Moses, Aaron and Aaron’s sons were to camp in front of the tabernacle, on the east, before the tent of meeting toward sunrise. They were to keep charge of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any unauthorized person who came near was to be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those camping in front of the tabernacle on the east, before the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and Aaron’s sons, keeping charge of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who approached was to be put to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves Aaron despite the extraordinary source dots and retains 22000 without harmonizing the earlier component counts.
verses.before: All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted at the command of the LORD, by their clans, every male from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
verses.after: The Levites registered by Moses and Aaron at the LORD’s direction, by their clans—all males one month old and upward—totaled 22,000.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted at the command of the LORD, by their clans, every male from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the firstborn male and age criteria and named registration, distinguishing this count from all Levites.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Count every firstborn male of the Israelites from one month old and upward, and record the number of their names.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Register every firstborn male among the Israelites one month old and upward, and list their names.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Count every firstborn male of the Israelites from one month old and upward, and record the number of their names.

verses.rationale: Retains the divine self-identification within the command and both human and livestock substitutions.
verses.before: You will take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.”
verses.after: Take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites, and take the Levites’ livestock in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites’ livestock.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the full firstborn scope and command-fulfillment formula after the quoted instructions.
verses.before: So Moses counted every firstborn among the Israelites, as the LORD commanded him.
verses.after: Moses registered all the firstborn among the Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses counted every firstborn among the Israelites, as the LORD commanded him.

verses.rationale: Retains the precise total, name registration, sex and age band required for the following redemption calculation.
verses.before: All the firstborn males, by the number of names from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
verses.after: The firstborn males registered by name, one month old and upward, totaled 22,273.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the firstborn males, by the number of names from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.

verses.rationale: Preserves the new speech introduction before the substitution and money instructions.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated substitution and ownership statement, including the shorter livestock wording here rather than replacing it with verse 41.
verses.before: “Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites will be mine. I am the LORD.
verses.after: “Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites, and the Levites’ livestock in place of their livestock. The Levites will belong to me. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites shall be mine. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact excess of 273 and the redemption purpose, leading directly into the amount in verse 47.
verses.before: For the redemption of the two hundred seventy-three firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,
verses.after: To redeem the 273 Israelite firstborn who exceed the number of the Levites,
verses.tsw_comparator: For the redemption of the two hundred seventy-three firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,

verses.rationale: Unfolds five-five/by-skull as an individual rate, retaining both ancient units and their explicit ratio.
verses.before: you will take five shekels for each person, according to the sanctuary shekel; the shekel is twenty gerahs.
verses.after: collect five shekels for each person, using the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall take five shekels for each person, according to the sanctuary shekel; the shekel is twenty gerahs.

verses.rationale: Makes the excess group’s referent clear, keeps silver rather than implying coins, and names both recipients.
verses.before: Give the money, the redemption price for people who exceed their number, to Aaron and his sons.”
verses.after: Give this silver to Aaron and his sons as the redemption payment for those who exceed the number of the Levites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Give the money, the redemption price for those who exceed their number, to Aaron and his sons.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the excess group as payers and the distinction between substitution and payment.
verses.before: So Moses took the redemption money from people who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
verses.after: Moses collected the redemption silver from those beyond the number redeemed by the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses took the redemption money from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact collection and sanctuary standard, matching 273 people at five shekels each.
verses.before: From the firstborn of the Israelites he took the money, one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
verses.after: He collected 1,365 shekels of silver from the Israelite firstborn, measured by the sanctuary shekel.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the firstborn of the Israelites he took the money, one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.

verses.rationale: Keeps both named recipients and the repeated divine-command conclusion, without shortening away its emphasis.
verses.before: Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons according to the word of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: Moses gave the redemption silver to Aaron and his sons at the LORD’s direction, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons according to the word of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves both recipients before the Kohathite service census.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps Kohath within Levi and both kinship levels, continuing the census criteria across the verse boundary.
verses.before: “Take a census of the Kohathites from among the Levites, by their clans and ancestral houses,
verses.after: “Take a census of the descendants of Kohath from among the Levites, by clan and ancestral household,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take a census of the Kohathites from among the Levites, by their clans and ancestral houses,

verses.rationale: Retains the thirty-to-fifty age range and renders tsava as organized sanctuary service here rather than military duty.
verses.before: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who enters the service to do the work at the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: from thirty years old up to fifty—all who enter the service to work at the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who enters the service to do the work at the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Renders the holy-of-holies phrase as the sacred objects described next, not permission to enter the inner chamber.
verses.before: This is the service of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting: the most holy things.
verses.after: The Kohathites’ work at the tent of meeting concerns the most holy things.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the service of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting: the most holy things.

verses.rationale: Keeps the priests as actors and the dividing curtain as the ark’s first covering before transport.
verses.before: When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons will go in and take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
verses.after: When the camp is ready to move, Aaron and his sons are to go in, take down the dividing curtain and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons shall go in and take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of the testimony with it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ark’s unique outer blue layer and sequence; retains uncertain taḥash and notes the pole instruction alongside Exodus 25:15.
verses.before: They will put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth entirely of blue on top, and insert its poles.
verses.after: They are to put a covering of taḥash skin over it, spread a cloth entirely of blue over that, and put its carrying poles in place.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth entirely of blue on top, and insert its poles.

verses.rationale: Retains all four vessel categories and their source order using the Exodus vocabulary; preserves the bread remaining with the table.
verses.before: Over the table of the Presence they will spread a blue cloth and place on it the plates, dishes, bowls, and jars for drink offerings; the regular bread will remain on it.
verses.after: They are to spread a blue cloth over the table of the Presence and place on it the dishes, ladles, bowls and pitchers for poured offerings. The regular bread is to remain on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the table of the Presence they shall spread a blue cloth and place on it the plates, dishes, bowls, and jars for drink offerings; the regular bread shall remain on it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the table’s scarlet layer distinct from the ark’s blue exterior and retains the skin and poles.
verses.before: They will spread a scarlet cloth over these, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and insert its poles.
verses.after: They are to spread a scarlet cloth over these things, cover it with taḥash skin and put its carrying poles in place.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall spread a scarlet cloth over these, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and insert its poles.

verses.rationale: Retains every lampstand component and oil vessel without compressing the inventory to accessories alone.
verses.before: They will take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, its lamps, tongs, trays, and all its oil vessels with which they tend it.
verses.after: They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for lighting, its lamps, tongs, firepans and all the oil containers used in its service.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, its lamps, tongs, trays, and all its oil vessels with which they tend it.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the mot transport bar from the fitted poles elsewhere; a note leaves its exact construction open.
verses.before: They will place it and all its utensils in a covering of fine leather and put it on the carrying frame.
verses.after: They are to wrap the lampstand and all its equipment in a covering of taḥash skin and place it on a carrying bar.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall place it and all its utensils in a covering of fine leather and put it on the carrying frame.

verses.rationale: Preserves the gold altar, blue/skin sequence and fitted poles as a separate inventory entry.
verses.before: Over the golden altar they will spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and insert its poles.
verses.after: They are to spread a blue cloth over the gold altar, cover it with taḥash skin and put its carrying poles in place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the golden altar they shall spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and insert its poles.

verses.rationale: Keeps all service utensils and each wrapping/transport step without specifying an unsupported transport design.
verses.before: They will take all the utensils of service used in the sanctuary, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and put them on the carrying frame.
verses.after: They are to gather all the utensils used for service in the sanctuary, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with taḥash skin and place them on a carrying bar.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall take all the utensils of service used in the sanctuary, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and put them on the carrying frame.

verses.rationale: Preserves removing ashes and the purple covering, distinguishing this altar’s preparation from the gold altar’s.
verses.before: They will remove the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
verses.after: They are to remove the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall remove the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

verses.rationale: Retains every tool, the repeated all-equipment phrase, outer skin and poles; does not import a basin addition absent from the pinned source.
verses.before: They will place on it all the utensils used in its service: the firepans, forks, shovels, basins, and all the utensils of the altar. They will spread over it a covering of fine leather and insert its poles.
verses.after: They are to put on it all the equipment used in its service: the firepans, forks, shovels and basins—all the altar’s equipment. Then they are to spread a covering of taḥash skin over it and put its carrying poles in place.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall place on it all the utensils used in its service: the firepans, forks, shovels, basins, and all the utensils of the altar. They shall spread over it a covering of fine leather and insert its poles.

verses.rationale: Makes covering-before-carrying explicit and keeps the warning of death from touching, distinct from an execution command.
verses.before: When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furnishings of the sanctuary as the camp sets out, then the Kohathites will come to carry them. But they will not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things the Kohathites will carry from the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: Once Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy things and all their sacred equipment when the camp moves, the Kohathites may come to carry them. They must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the loads the Kohathites are to carry for the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furnishings of the sanctuary as the camp sets out, then the Kohathites shall come to carry them. But they shall not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things the Kohathites shall carry from the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Retains all four entrusted supplies and the broader oversight, with no conflation of lighting oil and anointing oil.
verses.before: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest will have oversight of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil—oversight of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, including the sanctuary and its furnishings.”
verses.after: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is responsible for the lighting oil, fragrant incense, regular grain offering and anointing oil. He has oversight of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, its holy things and equipment.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall have oversight of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil—oversight of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, including the sanctuary and its furnishings.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed instruction to both leaders as a separate warning.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains cut-off language with permissive force in context, making the leaders’ protective responsibility audible.
verses.before: “Do not let the tribe of the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.
verses.after: “Do not let the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Do not let the tribe of the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.

verses.rationale: Keeps the positive and negative life/death purpose, priestly action and each man’s individually assigned work and burden.
verses.before: Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons will go in and assign each of them to their service and burden.
verses.after: Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his task and his load.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign each of them to their service and burden.

verses.rationale: Identifies the otherwise ambiguous they and retains the death warning; notes the alternative reading while the holy things are being covered.
verses.before: But the Kohathites will not go in to look at the holy things even for a moment, or they will die.”
verses.after: The Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Kohathites shall not go in to look at the holy things even for a moment, or they will die.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses alone as recipient for the Gershonite and Merarite instructions.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains as-well linking the groups, with the source’s household-then-clan order.
verses.before: “Take a census also of the Gershonites, by their ancestral houses and clans.
verses.after: “Take a census of Gershon’s descendants as well, by ancestral household and clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take a census also of the Gershonites, by their ancestral houses and clans.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated age limits and organized service criterion without confusing this count with chapter 3’s infants-and-up census.
verses.before: From thirty years old up to fifty years old you will count them, everyone who enters to perform service and do the work at the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: Register those from thirty years old up to fifty, all who enter the service to do the work of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: From thirty years old up to fifty years old you shall count them, everyone who enters to perform service and do the work at the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two aspects of work and transport and introduces the detailed list as one connected sentence.
verses.before: This is the service of the Gershonite clans, in serving and carrying:
verses.after: This is the work assigned to the Gershonite clans, both their service and what they are to carry:
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the service of the Gershonite clans, in serving and carrying:

verses.rationale: Retains curtains, tent, both coverings and entrance screen; does not collapse distinct fabric layers.
verses.before: they will carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering and the covering of fine leather that is over it, the screen for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
verses.after: They are to carry the tabernacle curtains and the tent of meeting, its covering and the taḥash covering above it, and the screen at the entrance of the tent of meeting,
verses.tsw_comparator: they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering and the covering of fine leather that is over it, the screen for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,

verses.rationale: Keeps the full courtyard inventory, ropes, tools and final all-work clause present in the Hebrew.
verses.before: the hangings of the court, the screen for the entrance of the court around the tabernacle and altar, their cords, and all the equipment for their service. Everything that is to be done with these will be their service.
verses.after: as well as the courtyard hangings and the screen at the gate of the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar, their ropes and all the equipment for their service. They are to do all the work needed for these things.
verses.tsw_comparator: the hangings of the court, the screen for the entrance of the court around the tabernacle and altar, their cords, and all the equipment for their service. Everything that is to be done with these shall be their service.

verses.rationale: Unfolds at-the-mouth as direction while retaining the repeated all-work/load scope and addressed leaders’ assignment responsibility.
verses.before: All the service of the Gershonites, all their carrying and all their work, will be at the command of Aaron and his sons. You will assign to them responsibility for everything they carry.
verses.after: All the Gershonites’ work, everything they carry and every task they perform, is to be directed by Aaron and his sons. You are to assign them responsibility for everything they carry.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the service of the Gershonites, all their carrying and all their work, shall be at the command of Aaron and his sons. You shall assign to them responsibility for everything they carry.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Ithamar’s immediate supervision from Aaron and sons’ direction in verse 27 and preserves his father’s identity.
verses.before: This is the service of the clans of the Gershonites at the Tent of Meeting, and their charge will be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
verses.after: This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the tent of meeting. Their responsibilities are under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the service of the clans of the Gershonites at the Tent of Meeting, and their charge shall be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

verses.rationale: Keeps the final clan group and both registration levels without adding a new divine speech.
verses.before: As for the Merarites, you will count them by their clans and ancestral houses.
verses.after: Register Merari’s descendants by clan and ancestral household.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the Merarites, you shall count them by their clans and ancestral houses.

verses.rationale: Preserves the same age band and sanctuary service criteria in the source’s repeated formula.
verses.before: From thirty years old up to fifty years old you will count them, everyone who enters the service to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: Register those from thirty years old up to fifty, all who enter the service to do the work of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: From thirty years old up to fifty years old you shall count them, everyone who enters the service to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps the load-as-charge relation and all four structural categories, continuing the list into verse 32.
verses.before: This is what they are responsible to carry for all their service at the Tent of Meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars, and bases,
verses.after: These are the things they are responsible for carrying in all their service at the tent of meeting: the tabernacle’s frames, crossbars, pillars and bases,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what they are responsible to carry for all their service at the Tent of Meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars, and bases,

verses.rationale: Retains small components and named item assignment; does not quietly shift by-name from equipment to personnel.
verses.before: the pillars around the court with their bases, pegs, and cords, together with all their equipment and everything related to their service. You will assign by name the objects they are responsible to carry.
verses.after: and the pillars around the courtyard, with their bases, pegs, ropes and all their equipment for every task. Assign by name the items they are responsible for carrying.
verses.tsw_comparator: the pillars around the court with their bases, pegs, and cords, together with all their equipment and everything related to their service. You shall assign by name the objects they are responsible to carry.

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete-service summary and Ithamar’s supervision, closing the instruction before the census report.
verses.before: This is the service of the clans of the Merarites for all their work at the Tent of Meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”
verses.after: This is the service of the Merarite clans, all their work at the tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the service of the clans of the Merarites for all their work at the Tent of Meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”

verses.rationale: Keeps all three categories of census takers and both kinship levels, linking to the age criterion in verse 35.
verses.before: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation counted the Kohathites by their clans and ancestral houses,
verses.after: Moses, Aaron and the community’s leaders registered the Kohathites by clan and ancestral household,
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation counted the Kohathites by their clans and ancestral houses,

verses.rationale: Retains the full repeated age and service scope in the report of compliance.
verses.before: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service for work at the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: from thirty years old up to fifty, all who entered the service to work at the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service for work at the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Preserves the exact Kohathite service count and its clan registration.
verses.before: Those counted by their clans were two thousand seven hundred fifty.
verses.after: Those registered by clan numbered 2,750.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those counted by their clans were two thousand seven hundred fifty.

verses.rationale: Keeps the group identification, all-serving scope and both census takers; through Moses distinguishes the command’s mediation.
verses.before: These were those counted of the Kohathite clans, everyone serving at the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
verses.after: These were the registered members of the Kohathite clans, all who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron registered them at the LORD’s command given through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were those counted of the Kohathite clans, everyone serving at the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the LORD through Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves the separate Gershonite report and connects its unfinished phrase to verse 39.
verses.before: Those counted of the Gershonites by their clans and ancestral houses,
verses.after: The descendants of Gershon were registered by clan and ancestral household,
verses.tsw_comparator: Those counted of the Gershonites by their clans and ancestral houses,

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated thirty-to-fifty criterion and sanctuary work, rather than replacing it with an abbreviated reference.
verses.before: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service for work at the Tent of Meeting,
verses.after: from thirty years old up to fifty, all who entered the service to work at the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service for work at the Tent of Meeting,

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact Gershonite service total and both kinship levels stated here.
verses.before: those counted by their clans and ancestral houses were two thousand six hundred thirty.
verses.after: Those registered by clan and ancestral household numbered 2,630.
verses.tsw_comparator: those counted by their clans and ancestral houses were two thousand six hundred thirty.

verses.rationale: Retains this group’s summary and both leaders without importing through Moses from the parallel Kohathite formula.
verses.before: These were those counted of the Gershonite clans, everyone serving at the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the LORD.
verses.after: These were the registered members of the Gershonite clans, all who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron registered them at the LORD’s command.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were those counted of the Gershonite clans, everyone serving at the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated clan/household grouping and continuation into the eligibility statement.
verses.before: Those counted of the Merarite clans by their clans and ancestral houses,
verses.after: The Merarite clans were registered by clan and ancestral household,
verses.tsw_comparator: Those counted of the Merarite clans by their clans and ancestral houses,

verses.rationale: Preserves the final group’s complete age and service criterion with matching English for the repeated Hebrew.
verses.before: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service for work at the Tent of Meeting,
verses.after: from thirty years old up to fifty, all who entered the service to work at the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service for work at the Tent of Meeting,

verses.rationale: Retains the exact Merarite service count and source’s clan-only wording here.
verses.before: those counted by their clans were three thousand two hundred.
verses.after: Those registered by clan numbered 3,200.
verses.tsw_comparator: those counted by their clans were three thousand two hundred.

verses.rationale: Preserves both leaders and the mediated command without adding the all-serving clause absent here.
verses.before: These were those counted of the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
verses.after: These were the registered members of the Merarite clans. Moses and Aaron registered them at the LORD’s command given through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were those counted of the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the LORD through Moses.

verses.rationale: Keeps the aggregate scope, three categories of census takers and both family levels, linked to the next verse.
verses.before: All the Levites whom Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted by their clans and ancestral houses,
verses.after: Moses, Aaron and Israel’s leaders registered all these Levites by clan and ancestral household,
verses.tsw_comparator: All the Levites whom Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted by their clans and ancestral houses,

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated age band and the summary’s distinction between service work and carrying work.
verses.before: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered to perform the work of service and the work of carrying at the Tent of Meeting,
verses.after: from thirty years old up to fifty, all who entered the service to do the work and carry the loads of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who entered to perform the work of service and the work of carrying at the Tent of Meeting,

verses.rationale: Preserves the aggregate service count, which agrees with 2750 plus 2630 plus 3200.
verses.before: those counted were eight thousand five hundred eighty.
verses.after: The total number registered was 8,580.
verses.tsw_comparator: those counted were eight thousand five hundred eighty.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the compressed final clause as a registration summary without silently changing the Hebrew; a note identifies its difficult syntax.
verses.before: According to the command of the LORD through Moses, each was counted according to service and burden. Thus they were counted, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: At the LORD’s command through Moses, each man was registered with his assigned task and load. Their registration followed what the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to the command of the LORD through Moses, each was counted according to service and burden. Thus they were counted, as the LORD commanded Moses.
